title: Cohort and dataset characteristics
notes: Percentages are donor-level, not cell-weighted. The ALL DATASETS row carries the analysis denominators: >=10 pericytes is the primary donor filter, >=20 the sensitivity filter. The cohorts do NOT carry equivalent metadata: `cell_count_basis` states what n_cells counts and `donor_metadata_available` names the donor attributes each source deposits, so a blank cell can be read as absent at source rather than as an omission. LungMAP in particular deposits only age, sex and batch, on a developmental age scale that is not comparable to the HLCA adult donors.

notes: Panels are IMPORTED from the modules that define them, not copied, so this table cannot fork from the code that built the scores. `n_state_programs` counts membership across the six primary programs only; BM subpanels are subsets of basement_membrane and would inflate the count. 0 of 102 curated genes are absent from the analysis object.

title: Stable pericyte cluster characteristics and program assignments
notes: Clusters are bootstrap-stable Leiden clusters on the study-integrated embedding, not marker-defined. `*_relenrich` is enrichment of a program score relative to the other clusters. Denoised AGTR1 is the Pericyte-only-trained scVI model. Per-cluster mean bootstrap Jaccard ranges 0.59-0.99 across the 6 clusters; the solution-level median of 0.966 conceals this spread, so per-cluster values should be cited rather than the median alone.

notes: BH ADDED HERE: neither source file carried an adjusted P. The donor-level CI is derived as estimate +/- 1.96*SE; the source CSV stored only estimate, se and p. Full model summaries with all covariate rows are in airspace_model_summary.txt and airspace_lmm_per_cell_summary.txt.

notes: Panel A rows are centred donor-aware program marginal means; panel B rows are donor x program pseudobulk correlations (n = 154). notes: Panel provenance: basement_membrane/_h/bm_panels.py. Detection statistics are within pericytes only.

notes: `p_BH_within_score` is the source file's `p.value`, renamed: emmeans::pairs was called with adjust = 'BH', so it is already adjusted across the 15 contrasts within each score and must NOT be adjusted again. title: Subpanel robustness of the basement-membrane program assignment
notes: Variants drop each BM subpanel in turn (collagen IV only, laminin only, linker only) and remove the shared COL4A1 from the fibroblast-like contrast panel. `flipped` marks a cluster whose dominant program changes under the variant.

notes: Outcomes are the basement-membrane score, the fibrillar- collagen score, their difference, and the BM score orthogonalized against the frozen fibrillar_ecm panel. The scVI-denoised lens is the AGTR1 readout; the raw and detection lenses are carried as the dropout-sensitive comparison and must not be read as the answer. The TGF-beta response panel shares no gene with either matrix panel or with any pericyte_states program (asserted in basement_membrane/_h/bm_panels.py), so the association is not arithmetic.

title: NicheNet ligand prioritization for the pericyte injury program
notes: All 321 ranked candidate ligands. `aupr_corrected` is the ranking statistic. A sender population counts as expressing a ligand at fraction >= 0.1, the same threshold 02.nichenet.R used. `ligand_class` is curated by hand: the repo's gene_program_detection.tsv covers only 34 panel genes and is missing seven of the eleven prioritized ligands.

title: Matched-gene-set specificity of the prioritized ligands (injury target set)
notes: Top 25 ligands against 1000 matched random target sets. The empirical P floor is 1/(1000+1) = 0.000999; every prioritized ligand sits at the floor, i.e. no null replicate reached the observed AUPR. Do NOT compare this floor with Table S11, which used 10,000 permutations.

title: Donor-level validation of the predicted sender-to-pericyte association
notes: TWO SPECIFICATIONS, both published, on different figures: lm(+dataset fixed) is Figure 4D, where the panel is a partial-regression plot whose drawn slope IS this coefficient; lmer(+1|dataset) is Figure S8C. They give materially different estimates and must not be quoted interchangeably. BH is applied within each model family.

title: Robustness of ligand prioritization to the definition of the receiver population
notes: Receiver schemes: whole pericytes, the three stable dominant-program receivers, and the five CoGAPS-defined receivers. `topk_overlap` uses k = 20.

title: Ligand prioritization against the basement-membrane target set
notes: All 321 candidate ligands against the basement-membrane genes expressed in pericytes (12 of the 20-gene panel; read the count from the run log, do not assume it), with 10,000 matched random target sets -- ten times the injury-set analysis, so the empirical P floor is 1/(10,000+1) = 9.999e-05. `rank_frozen` is the injury-program rank, so rank_change is positive when a ligand matters less for BM than for injury.

title: Comparison of basement-membrane and injury-program ligand rankings
notes: RECOMPUTED for this table: these summary statistics existed only as prose in bm_nichenet_README.txt. A modest rank correlation with partial top-20 overlap is the evidence for a partly distinct predicted regulatory architecture.

title: Full ligand-to-basement-membrane-target regulatory-potential matrix
notes: Complete 321 ligands x 12 targets = 3852 pairs, sliced directly from the NicheNet prior regulatory-potential matrix. IMPORTANT: the target set is the 12 basement-membrane genes expressed in pericytes above the 0.10 threshold, not all 13 -- LAMA3, LAMA5, AGRN fall below the receiver expression threshold and were never in the tested gene set. `shown_in_figure_heatmap` marks the 27 links the Figure S9D heatmap displays, which are the pairs surviving get_weighted_ligand_target_links(n = 200) plus the 0.33 visualization cutoff. The matrix is dense, so absolute weights are only meaningful relative to other pairs; the two rank columns give that comparison.

title: Ligand prioritization toward basement-membrane versus fibrillar-collagen targets
notes: Both columns come from the same script, priors, receiver and expression threshold; only geneset_oi differs, so the two rankings are comparable. Compare `perm_z`, not `aupr_corrected`: each z is standardised against its own target set's null of equally sized random gene sets drawn from the same receiver background, whereas AUPR still scales with target-set size. Spearman rank correlation between the two rankings: 0.347 over 321 ligands. The fibrillar target set is small, so its individual estimates are noisy -- read it as a comparison of ligand ORDERING, not of absolute activity.

title: Cell-type expression landscape of the local lung renin-angiotensin machinery
notes: `detect` is the donor-level detection fraction and `emmean` the depth-adjusted marginal expression with donor and study random effects. Within-gene ranks are computed here for all 22 populations; the stored ras_top_celltypes.tsv keeps only the top 3.

title: Circuit-role classification: completeness of the angiotensin II axis per cell type
notes: Roles are called at a donor-level detection threshold of 0.05. `n_core_roles` counts the three requirements (substrate, AngII-generating protease, AT1 receptor) and is computed here: the stored `n_steps_present` counts all five step columns and therefore cannot support the 'no cell type carried more than one requirement' claim. `chymase_gene` records which of CMA1/CTSG won the max() the source script discarded.
